top_signals.title: Oil Prices Climb Above $106 as Iran Threatens More Tanker Attacks
top_signals.summary: Crude oil prices moved higher earlier today, after Iranian officials told Reuters the country’s forces were planning to further intensify strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, deploying new tactics. Brent crude was trading at $106.37 per barrel, and West Texas Intermediate was trading at $94.72 per barrel, with the news that Israel’s Benjamin Netanyahu had asked Trump to start bombing Iran again likely to also contribute to the price rise. top_signals.title: Oman Overtakes U.S. as India's Top LNG Supplier in September
top_signals.summary: Oman was India’s single biggest LNG supplier in September, toppling the United States that held the top spot for months after the Iran war began, as European buyers are snapping up American cargoes and intensifying the competition of spot U.S. supply with Asia. The arbitrage economics have worked in Europe’s favor in recent weeks in attracting U.S. LNG cargoes, and European buyers gobbled up additional American supply amid historically low levels in gas storage sites across the EU ahead of the winter.
